summary.verdict: The implementation conforms to the Quality / Fitness Evaluation Engine contract: it evaluates identity-resolved records against phase contracts, emits QualityRecord, FitnessScore, QualityFlag and DisqualificationReason outputs, preserves input immutability, provenance, lineage, versioning, rule-version references and deterministic score bounds, and does not normalize, repair, mutate records, resolve identity or edit contracts. No material contract, boundary, metadata integrity or responsibility-separation violations were found.

test_results.coverage_assessment: Inline conformance smoke coverage exercised the documented happy path, input immutability, required output lineage metadata, malformed collection rejection, critical traceability disqualification and ambiguous identity warning behavior. The declared test specification also covers sparse valid inputs, malformed item and contract rejection, empty valid batches, exact threshold behavior, blocking flags with high total score and fail criteria for input mutation or out-of-scope normalization.
test_results.notes: Reviewed functional_contract.md, operational_rules.md, technical_schema.md, test_spec.md, failure_modes_spec.md, usage_example.md and the Python codebase. The engine validates list-shaped input collections, record identifiers, identity status, contract identifiers, contract versions, required fields and fitness thresholds before scoring. It selects an applicable active phase contract, computes completeness, traceability, contract consistency and fitness scores deterministically, clamps scores to the 0.0 to 1.0 range, emits structured QualityFlag records for missing required fields, missing provenance, missing lineage, ambiguous identity, restricted use, contract mismatch and threshold failures, and forces disqualification with a non-null DisqualificationReason when blocking flags exist. Deep-copy snapshots verified that evaluated records and contracts are not silently mutated.
